facts.statement: Martharaptor lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah.
facts.quote: Martharaptor is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UMNH VP 21400 was found at the Hayden-Corbett site, about eight miles southeast of Green River, Utah.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, UMNH VP 21400, hails from the Hayden-Corbett site of the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah, approximately eight miles southeast from the city of Green River.

facts.statement: The genus name Martharaptor honors paleontologist assistant Martha C. Hayden, and the species name greenriverensis refers to the Green River.
facts.quote: The generic name, Martharaptor, is in honor to the paleontologist assistant Martha C. Hayden who helped in the discovery of the site, and the specific name, greenriverensis, is a reference to the Green River.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen includes vertebrae, a scapula, limb bones, an ischium, and well-preserved hand claws.
facts.quote: The specimen includes fragments of vertebrae, a scapula, forelimb and hindlimb bones, and an ischium. It also includes well-preserved manual unguals.

facts.statement: Martharaptor is distinguished by skeletal features in the hands and feet that are intermediate between early therizinosauroids and advanced therizinosaurids.
facts.quote: They can be distinguished from other therizinosauroids by means of several features of the skeleton (particularly the hands and feet) which were intermediate between early therizinosaurs such as Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus, and more "advanced" members of the group like therizinosaurids.

facts.statement: The hand claws of Martharaptor are distinctive, with height greater than length and strong curvature.
facts.quote: The manual unguals (hand claws) are very distinctive. Their height is greater than their length, and they are strongly curved.

facts.statement: One preserved hand claw is larger and likely from the first finger, while the second and third finger claws are equal in size.
facts.quote: One of the preserved unguals is larger than the others, and it may represent the claw of the first finger. Other unguals are as large as each other, indicating that the second and third fingers had claws of equal size.

facts.statement: The fourth metatarsal is beveled, a feature intermediate between Falcarius and therizinosaurids.
facts.quote: The fourth metatarsal is beveled (slightly slopes to the side) compared to the rest of the foot. This is intermediate between Falcarius, which has no slope, and therizinosaurids, which have a fourth metatarsal angled at 90 degrees to the rest of the foot.

facts.statement: Preserved vertebral fragments include parts of a neck vertebra, a back vertebra, and a tail vertebra.
facts.quote: Three vertebral fragments are preserved. These include a strip of bone from the upper portion of a cervical (neck) vertebra, the centrum (main body) of a dorsal (back) vertebra, and the lower portion of a vertebra believed to be a distal caudal (i.e. from the tip of the tail).

facts.statement: If Martharaptor is a basal therizinosaur, the holotype was approximately 2.5 meters long and weighed 40 kilograms.
facts.quote: Martharaptor fue un terópodo pequeño bípedo. Su forma depende de a qué grupo pertenece el animal en realidad. Si es, como el artículo descriptivo mantiene, un terizinosaurio basal, entonces el tamaño del holotipo es de aproximadamente 2,5 metros y 40 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The skull of Martharaptor is unknown.
facts.quote: El cráneo es desconocido.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Martharaptor within Therizinosauroidea as the sister taxon to the Alxasaurus + Therizinosauridae group, though support is weak.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis placed Martharaptor within Therizinosauroidea as the sister taxon to the Alxasaurus + Therizinosauridae group, although support for this placement is weak.

facts.statement: Martharaptor greenriverensis lived in the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 124 million years ago during the Aptian stage in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Martharaptor greenriverensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Martharaptor de dinosaurio terópodo terizinosaurio que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 124 millones de años durante el Aptiense en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The hand claws are so strong that their curved length from the tip to a right angle on the back surface is less than the height of that back surface.
facts.quote: Las garras de mano son tan fuertes que su longitud curvada de la línea de punta en un ángulo recto a la superficie trasera es menor que la altura de dicha superficie trasera.

facts.statement: The first metatarsal touches the top of the ankle without flattening, unlike most theropods.
facts.quote: El primer hueso metatarsiano toca la parte superior del tobillo sin aplanar como la mayoría de los terópodos.

facts.statement: The first toe presumably had no function, similar to later Therizinosauridae.
facts.quote: El primer dedo no había presumiblemente tienen ninguna función como en los posteriores Therizinosauridae.

facts.statement: The species Martharaptor greenriverensis was named and described in 2012 by Philip Senter, James Kirkland, and Deblieux Donald.
facts.quote: En 2012, fue nombrada y descrita la especie tipo Martharaptor greenriverensis por Philip Senter, James Kirkland y Deblieux Donald.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UMNH VP 21400 dates to the early Aptian, approximately 124 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, UMNH VP 21400, fue encontrado en un estrato de la parte superior del Miembro Yellow Cat de la Formación Cedar Mountain, capa que data de principios de Aptiano, hace unos 124 millones de años.

facts.statement: The fossilized remains represented a small theropod that appeared to be an unknown species.
facts.quote: Se encontró el esqueleto de un terópodo pequeño que parecía representar una especie desconocida.

facts.statement: The fossil material includes vertebrae from the rear neck and tail, a scapula, ischium, pubis, and some elements of the forearm and foot.
facts.quote: Incluye vértebras de la parte posterior del cuello y la cola, una escápula, un isquion, pubis y algunos elementos del antebrazo y del pie.

facts.statement: The find consisted of loose bones scattered over an area of one square meter at a depth of twenty centimeters.
facts.quote: El hallazgo se compone de huesos sueltos en un área de un metro cuadrado a una profundidad de veinte centímetros.

facts.statement: The describers placed Martharaptor within the group Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: Martharaptor fue colocado por los descriptores dentro de Therizinosauroidea.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis placed Martharaptor in a basal position, above Beipiaosaurus but below Alxasaurus on the family tree.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con un análisis cladistico se encontró en una posición basal, sobre Beipiaosaurus pero por debajo de Alxasaurus en el árbol genealógico.

facts.statement: The describers noted that the phylogenetic position was very uncertain due to the poor quality of the findings.
facts.quote: Los descriptores señalaron sin embargo, que la ubicación debido a lo pobre de los hallazgos era muy incierta.

facts.statement: Typical therizinosaur characteristics include strongly curved relatively narrow claws and the absence of hinge joints in the mid-foot bones.
facts.quote: Las características típicas de los terizinosaurios son la fuerte curvatura de las garras relativamente estrechos y la ausencia de articulaciones de bisagra en los huesos medio pie.

facts.statement: The genus lived during the Valanginian stage, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The first metatarsal thins toward the ankle, indicating the first toe did not contact the ground.
rejected.quote: The first metatarsal thins towards the ankle, similar to most theropods but unlike therizinosaurids, indicating that the first toe did not contact the ground.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the first toe did not contact the ground'

rejected.statement: The preserved scapula has a hatchet-like shape expanded near the shoulder and measures about 15 cm long.
rejected.quote: The only preserved bone of the pectoral girdle is the left scapula (shoulder blade). This bone has a hatchet-like shape, expanded near the shoulder as in other therizinosauroids which preserve a scapula and measures about 15 cm long.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'has a hatchet-like shape expanded near the shoulder'

rejected.statement: The holotype was discovered 15 kilometers southeast of Rio Verde in eastern Utah by Martha Hayden and Cari Corbett.
rejected.quote: Fue encontrado a quince kilómetros al sureste de Río Verde en el este de Utah por Martha Hayden y Cari Corbett en un sitio de dinosaurios.
